messages:
emma: Found a reproducible issue in the Android sample app: coroutine cancellation + Retrofit suspend call leaves OkHttp dispatcher threads stuck on older Android (8/9). Hangs happen during streaming response. Anyone seen this?

raj: Yes. Does the suspend adapter call Call.timeout().cancel()? Retrofit's adapter sometimes only calls Call.cancel().

emma: We're on retrofit 2.9.0 + okhttp 4.9.2. Snippet:
```kotlin
withTimeout(1200) { api.streamLarge() } // suspend call
```
Client has readTimeout disabled, callTimeout 30s.

li: Do you use HTTP/2? I've seen HTTP/2 frame reader threads stay blocked on some Android kernels even after cancel.

emma: Default HTTP/2 is on. Forcing Protocol.HTTP_1_1 in OkHttp client makes the issue go away in my device tests.

raj: Workarounds: 1) set a small readTimeout in CI, 2) force HTTP_1_1 for device tests, 3) patch suspend adapter to call call.timeout().cancel() before call.cancel(), or 4) in EventListener close the socket on cancel. All are imperfect.

emma: Tried calling call.timeout().cancel(); call.cancel() but still saw occasional stuck reads on Android 8.1 emulator. Closing socket from EventListener helped tests but noisy in logs.

li: Can you try OkHttp 5.x snapshot? They tweaked HTTP/2 shutdown semantics.

emma: Will try and attach a minimal sample app + thread dump to an internal issue. For onboarding docs we should call out: "If you rely on per-request coroutine cancellations on Android <=9, consider forcing HTTP/1.1 or bounding readTimeouts in CI/device tests."

build-bot: Device tests failed: android-8-emulator  dispatcher thread exhaustion. Logs: https://ci.internal/7890

raj: Thanks, filing INT-4512 and pinging eng-runtime.

emma: Filing sample repo as gist and linking INT-4512. Will report results with OkHttp 5. :pray:
